hanna.title: The Off-Duty Ledger
hanna.text:
Hanna traps you at a corner table in the bakery with two mugs of cider and a thick sheaf of guild forms. She's annotated them in bright blue ink.

"Business meeting," she says. "Very serious. Sit."

Half the pages are real. They're bounty tallies, with her corrections. The other half are something else. There's a hand-drawn seating chart of the guild hall. It shows which adventurers tip best, which merchants blush when you compliment them, and who has been seen leaving whose room.

In one margin there's a small doodle of a hooded figure. It's labeled "Terrible disguise. 10/10 charm."

You're reading it upside down. She catches you and slaps the paper flat. The freckles across her nose have gone bright pink.

"Trade secrets! Eyes on your pastry, Sam!" She pulls the whole stack toward her side of the table. "That one's old, anyway. It's from before I knew you. I've got much better material now."
ngpp: Next to the hooded doodle she stops and squints at her own ink. "Huh," she mutters. "I could have sworn I drew a little lantern beside that." She taps the page with her pencil, shrugs, and tells herself she's just tired from the night shift.

"Okay, creepy question," she says over her cider, squinting at her ink. "Did I already tell you the hoodie disguise joke? Why did my hand write 'still 10/10' under it? I never wrote that. Don't look at me like I'm the one being weird."

"Don't laugh," she says, and slides the blue ink ledger halfway toward you. "Every page in this stack reads like notes from a life we already lived, Sam. I know what's on the next page. I wrote it down, I think, and then it got lost. Tell me I'm not losing it."

choices.label: Demand to see the rest of your margin notes
choices.res: You reach for the stack and she swats your hands away. She fails, and ends up laughing into her cider, one hand holding the ledger down. Then she gives you a wildly exaggerated, dramatic reading of every rumor she's ever heard about you, with voices. The baker looks over. She doesn't stop. By the end her freckles are bright pink, and she has not once looked at the real pages.

choices.label: Ask why she really left the Guild desk
choices.res: Her grin softens into something real. "Because standing behind a counter hearing everyone else's stories gets old, Sam," she says. She turns her mug a quarter turn on the table. "I knew the whole town's business and none of it was mine. I wanted to actually live in one, for a change." She looks at you, and doesn't joke. The cider goes cold between you.

image.comp: leaning over a bakery table shielding a stack of annotated parchment sheets, freckled cheeks flushed, laughing brightly
image.setting: warm corner bakery table by a sunlit window, mugs of cider

hanna.title: Filing Error
hanna.text:
You open the washroom door on the assumption that nobody is in there.

Hanna is perched on the rim of the tub in a thin towel. One damp blonde curl is plastered across her eyebrow. She has a stack of soaked index cards, and she's drying them one at a time over a candle stub.

She yelps. The cards very nearly go back into the water.

Then she recovers, and narrows her eyes at you. It's pure theater.

"Knock much?! I could have been doing anything in here!" She's holding a card over the flame by one corner. It's starting to smoke. "And before you ask, no, these aren't about you."

She looks at the card in her hand.

"Mostly."

She turns it face down on her knee. You saw the first word on it before she did, and it was your name.

1.text:
You push open the washroom door. Hanna is sitting sideways on the rim of the bath in a short towel, with wet curls sticking to her freckles. She puts her stack of cards down, dry side up.

She doesn't yelp. She gives you a sly, breathless grin, and hooks one finger into the pocket of your hoodie.

"Terrible timing, Sam." She tugs you a step closer. "Unless you've finally come to give me that interview. I've got a lot of questions, and I'd rather not ask them with my clothes on. I do my best work face to face."

choices.label: Step into the steam and claim her live interview at the tub rim
choices.res: You step into the steam and she tips her face up to you. Her wet curls are cold against your wrist. You put a hand behind her neck and she lets you hold her there. "Best filing error all week," she breathes, and her hand slides into the pocket of your hoodie and stays. You kiss her, and the candle gutters.

choices.label: Leave her to dry her cards with a promise for later
choices.res: You tell her to take her time with the cards, and promise her the interview later. She goes pink to the ears. "I'm holding you to that after hours," she calls brightly behind the latch. She is trying to sound casual, and she is not. You hear her laugh once, alone, and then the scrape of a stool.

image.comp: sitting sideways on the rim of the bath in a short towel, wet curls on freckles, hooking a finger in his pocket and tugging him closer, sly breathless grin

3.text:
You open the washroom door. Hanna is up to her chest in hot bubbles, with her wet gold hair piled up and one curl hanging over her grin.

She sees you. She lifts one bare foot out of the water, sets it against the door, and kicks the latch shut herself. Then she stands up in the tub. Foam slides down off her tits and her stomach, and she lets you watch it go.

"Knock? Please. You know the bath schedule by heart." She crooks a finger. "Get your shirt off and get in here, Sam. I've been thinking about your cock all afternoon, and the water won't stay hot forever."

choices.label: Climb straight into the steaming bath under her
choices.res: You pull your shirt off and she watches every inch of it with a grin. The water is hot as you climb in. She lowers herself into your lap, wet thighs settling astride your hips in the bubbles, and she laughs softly against your lips. "Told you," she says. "It won't stay hot forever." Her hands are already in your hair.

choices.label: Wash the soap across her shoulders and tease her about gossip
choices.res: You take the soap and wash it across her shoulders instead, and tease her about gossip. She melts back against your chest with a happy groan and tips her head to give you her neck. "Okay," she says. "Better than any ledger." She's slow and loose in your hands. She tells you three rumors and forgets the third.

image.comp: standing up in a bubble bath, foam sliding off her breasts and stomach, wet hair piled up, crooking a finger, cheeky grin

choices.label: Apologize and shut the door fast
choices.res: You apologize and shut the door fast. "Smooth exit!" she calls through the wood, and you hear a wet card slap onto the tiles. Five minutes later she slides a single dry index card under your door. It reads: IOUs, 1 proper knock (collectable tonight). The handwriting is steady. The underline isn't.

choices.label: Ask which card has your name on it
choices.res: You ask which card has your name on it. Hanna smirks and lets the towel dip an inch at her collarbone. She holds a card between two fingers, just out of reach. "Depends," she says. "Are you offering a live interview?" Her eyes don't leave your face. She tucks the card against her chest, and she is, for once, in no hurry at all.

else.res: "Classified!" she announces, and throws a wet sponge straight at your chest. It hits with a slap. You step back, and she slams the latch shut with a bright laugh. You hear her bump into the stool, and then you hear her whispering something to herself that sounds a lot like your name.

choices.label: Offer to hold the candle so she doesn't burn the cards
choices.res: You offer to hold the candle so she doesn't burn the cards. "Now that's executive support," she says with a grin, and tugs the towel tight around her thighs. You lean on the doorframe and hold the stub steady while she dries the cards one by one. She keeps the one with your name face down on her knee the whole time.

image.comp: perched on the rim of a wooden bath wrapped in a towel, holding damp index cards near a candle, startled playful grin

hanna.title: After Last Call
hanna.text:
The common room is dark except for one low lantern behind the counter. Hanna is sitting on a tall stool with her shoes off, swinging her legs and counting the night's tips into neat brass stacks.

She's been talking since you came down. It's about the cook's feud with the fishmonger, and a knight who has been in three times this week and won't say why.

You lean on the bar beside her. The talking slows down, and then it stops.

She reaches out and straightens your collar with light, warm fingers. She doesn't take her hand away afterward.

"Funny thing," she says quietly. She's looking at your shirt button and not at your eyes. "I spent five years at that desk writing down everybody else's secrets. I knew the whole town's business. Nobody knew a thing about me. I made sure of it." Her thumb moves on your collar. "I never realized how nice it'd be when somebody already knew mine."

choices.label: Cover her hand with yours on your collar
choices.res: You cover her hand with yours where it rests on your collar. Her fingers curl into your shirt at once, and her freckles glow in the amber light. "Yeah," she whispers. She leans forward until her forehead rests against your chin, and stays there. The coins sit uncounted. She doesn't say another word about the knight.

choices.label: Lock the front bolt and lift her onto the empty bar
choices.res: You throw the front bolt and come back to her. You lift her onto the empty bar and brass coins clatter across the counter. She laughs, breathless, and hooks her ankles behind your waist. "I just counted those," she says. Her hands pull your shirt free, and she tips your mouth down to hers. The lantern is the only light left.

choices.label: Pour two nightcaps and stay by the counter
choices.res: You pour two nightcaps and stay by the counter. She hops down to sit on the bar beside you, and bumps her knee against yours. The quiet house settles around you both. She sips, and doesn't tell you anything for a while, which for Hanna is a gift. When she leans on your shoulder, you let her.

image.comp: sitting on a dark wooden bar counter barefoot by a single lantern, adjusting his collar with a quiet tender smile
image.setting: quiet pleasure-house bar after closing, single amber lantern

hanna.title: Head Clerkship
hanna.text:
A messenger from the Adventurers' Guild comes by before noon with a letter stamped in red wax.

The head clerk has retired. The Guildmaster wants Hanna back. He's offering double her old pay, a corner office of her own, and a seat on the trade council.

She reads it twice on the front steps. She's twirling her pencil between her knuckles as she goes, faster and faster, and on the second read-through it snaps in half.

She looks up at you. For once there's no teasing in her face.

"It's everything I thought I wanted, two years ago," she says softly. "I used to lie awake planning what I'd do with that office. I had the curtains picked out."

She turns the two halves of the pencil over in her palm.

"I walked out because I was sick of knowing everybody's story and not having one. I've got one now. Say the word, Sam. What do you think I should do?"
ngpp: She stares at the red wax and snaps her pencil on the beat, then blinks down at the two halves. She remembers the sound of it. She doesn't say so. She sets the pieces down on the step and straightens them with one finger.

"Weirdest déjà vu," she mutters over the offer letter. "Why does double pay already sound like bad news compared to staying on your porch? I haven't even finished reading it." She looks at you sideways. "I think I've turned this down. I'd like to say it out loud and see."

"Look at me holding a fancy corner office scroll and already tearing the corner," she says quietly, and her freckles are warm. "I already chose you over that marble desk once, Sam. Didn't even have to think. I'm not weighing it this time. I'm just telling you I know."

choices.label: "I'd hate to lose you, yet I won't hold you back."
choices.res: You tell her you'd hate to lose her and you won't hold her back. Hanna exhales slowly and laughs, a little wetly. Then she crumples the red wax offer into her pocket. "Good answer, Sam. Mostly because I'd already decided not to go," she says. She wipes her eye with her wrist, and then she punches your arm, once, lightly.

choices.label: "Stay here with me. This place isn't half as bright without you."
choices.res: You tell her to stay, and that this place isn't half as bright without her. Her face lights up bright enough to outshine the porch lantern. She grabs the messenger's ink pen and scribbles across the bottom of the letter: Position already filled, by me, somewhere better. She hands it back to him with a flourish and kisses you on the cheek.

choices.label: "Double pay is hard to argue with."
choices.res: You say double pay is hard to argue with. Her smile goes flat in half a second. "Right. Good business sense," she says. She walks inside without waiting for you. She doesn't slam anything. When morning comes she is still behind your desk, quiet and unusually distant, sorting receipts into neat piles, and she doesn't tease you once.

image.comp: standing on porch steps holding an official red-wax guild letter and a snapped pencil, serious hopeful expression
image.setting: lantern-lit wooden front steps in daylight

hanna.title: Off the Market
hanna.text:
Hanna drags you up the bell tower above the market street just before sunset. She's got a bag of warm honey almonds, and she sits down at the overlook with it between her knees.

The evening lamps are coming on all across Hollowmere. Down below, the guild hall doors open, and the adventurers spill out toward tavern row in twos and threes.

She used to know every one of them. She could have told you their tabs and who they were sweet on. From up here she could still point out who's avoiding whom.

She leans her head on your shoulder and sighs.

"Look at them all," she says lazily. "Sixteen parties. I can count about forty rumors from here. See those two by the fountain? Something's definitely going on there." She eats an almond. "And for once I don't care. I've spent my whole life watching other people's stories from behind a counter. The best one in town is sitting right next to me, and I'm in it."

choices.label: Kiss her temple and pull her closer
choices.res: You kiss her temple and pull her closer. She turns her face up before you can pull away and catches your mouth, and it is a warm, sweet kiss that tastes like honey and dusk. The almond bag tips over between her knees and neither of you picks it up. Down in the square, the lamps keep coming on, one by one.

choices.label: Tell her you're glad she walked out on the Guild
choices.res: You tell her you're glad she walked out on the Guild. "Best impulse decision I ever made," she says happily, and she laces her fingers tight through yours. She doesn't tease you about it. She points out the two by the fountain, and then, quietly, she stops pointing at anyone, and you watch the stars come out together.

image.comp: sitting on a stone tower ledge at sunset leaning her head on his shoulder, overlooking a lantern-lit fantasy town
image.setting: stone clocktower overlook at sunset above glowing city rooftops

hanna.title: Front Page
hanna.text:
Hanna shuts your bedroom door with her heel and leans back against it.

She's wearing your spare shirt and nothing else. It comes halfway down her thighs. She's grinning, bright-eyed and out of breath, and the sight of her goes through you like heat.

She crosses the rug in four steps and climbs into your lap on the edge of the bed. Her hands come up to frame your face.

"I've been writing this down all week," she whispers. "I couldn't get it right, so I'm just going to say it."

She presses her forehead to yours. Her hips settle against you.

"No more margin notes. No more rumors. I'm done standing behind somebody else's counter and writing about what other people get." Her breath is warm on your mouth. "I want the whole thing, Sam. Every week, every cycle, and nothing kept back. I know everybody's secret in this town. Mine is that I'm in love with you. Tell me I'm yours."
ngpp: Buttoned in nothing but your oversized shirt, she pauses mid stride on the rug. A flash of heat goes over her face, and she doesn't know why. She presses her hand flat to her chest, laughs at herself, and closes the last few steps.

"Okay, laugh at me," she says against your chin, her hips settling in your lap. "Why does straddling you in this shirt already feel like my favorite habit? I've never done this. I know exactly where my knees go." Her grin is shaky, and her hands are not.

"Reset the cycle all she wants," Hanna says, and undoes the first button of the stolen shirt under your hands. "My body never forgot this bed, Sam. I know what I said last time. I'm saying it again, on the record. Put me on the front page tonight."
hanna.goLead: You peel your shirt up off Hanna's freckled shoulders and lay her back on the sheets. She's laughing, and then the laugh turns into a low, eager gasp against your throat.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.res: Hanna blinks and swallows hard, and manages a crooked smile as she climbs off your lap. "Okay," she says softly, and pulls the oversized shirt tighter around herself. "Wait's on the record." She fetches her boots from the rug and doesn't put them on. "Just don't keep a girl on hold too long. I'm bad at it."
